_meta.description: Canonical navigation layout applied AFTER all manifest.d fragments merge (see applyMenuRelocations in main.js). Fragments stay the source of WHAT exists in the menu (ADR-037); this file is the single place deciding WHERE entries live. relocations: sourceId -> targetGroupId (groups dissolve into the target, leaves move under it, a child group targeting its own parent flattens) — this is how an entry is re-homed, and it MOVES navigation rather than deleting it. settingsSection: ids lifted into Nextcloud's settings foldout. removals: now EMPTY — see _removals_note for why the previous 160 entries were withdrawn; ADR-044 (no-functionality-loss) requires that retiring a menu entry leave its route reachable from some other surviving entry, which must be checked per id before this list is ever repopulated. Lives outside manifest.json because the app-manifest-v2 schema has additionalProperties:false at the root.

_relocations_nav_six_clusters_note: nav-six-clusters (2026-08-20): the 29 pre-restructure top-level groups fold into Dashboard + 6 clusters (Bookkeeping, Sales, Purchasing, BankingCashflow, Taxes, ReportingCompliance — the last two are RENAMED ids, formerly Belastingen/Compliance, edited directly in src/manifest.json since REQ-NAVC-001 scenario 2 requires the OLD ids not survive as top-level entries). Any existing relocation whose TARGET was itself a folding id (BankingTreasury, Payroll, PublicSector, Subsidies — all had children:[] in the base and existed only to receive these) is retargeted DIRECTLY to the final cluster id rather than chained through the folding id, per design.md §5/REQ-NAVC-006's own 140-orphan lesson: applyMenuRelocations resolves a single hop per id per pass, so `X -> FoldingId` plus `FoldingId -> Cluster` in the SAME relocations map races the pass in which FoldingId itself dissolves and orphans X at the top level for good (verified against this repo's own buildManifest.js — the dissolving group is removed from the top-level array during the SAME scan pass that discovers X's move, so `menu.find(target)` fails and X falls back to a bare top-level push, and once FoldingId is gone it never reappears for a later pass to retry against).
_settingsSection_note: Ids lifted into Nextcloud's settings foldout (the bottom-left gear / NcAppNavigationSettings, OUTSIDE the scrollable nav) by applySettingsSection in main.js — each becomes a flat top-level item with section:'settings'. This is the special settings position, not a normal menu group. ⚠️ THESE ARE MENU IDS, NOT PAGE IDS. An id here that matches no menu entry is INERT — it lifts nothing and reports nothing. That is exactly what happened to External Connections: the list carried the PAGE id `ExternalAdaptersStatus` while the MENU id is `ExternalConnections`, so the intended demotion silently did nothing and the entry kept its top-level slot. It was the only inert id in this list; verify a new id against the merged menu before adding it.
_removals_note: ADR-112: a report is a card on the Reporting & Compliance page OR a menu entry, never both. All six pages stay routable — deep links, e2e specs and the cards address them by route name — only their menu entries go. Five were already declared as cards in src/components/reporting/reportViews.js when that file was written from the menu-IA audit; BookkeepingDestructionReport was missed there, so it is added as a card in the same change that retires its entry. Retiring an entry whose card did not exist would have removed the report from the product rather than moving it.
